gp.text: Cost of revenue and gross margin- RPD. Cost of revenue increased by $271,799 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from the three months ended September 30, 2025 and by $1,420,371 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Gross margin increased $584,026 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from the three months ended September 30, 2025 and $1,976,311 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the relocation of the Company’s facility. During 2025, the Company was in the process of relocating operations and as a result, was operating at a limited capacity. Following the completion of the relocation the business returned to normal operating capacity resulting in higher revenue levels and related costs. The year-over-year increase is also impacted by the timing of the common control transaction. The statement of operations for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 includes operating activity from April 16, 2025 only, compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

cor.text: Cost of revenue and gross margin- RPD. Cost of revenue increased by $271,799 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from the three months ended September 30, 2025 and by $1,420,371 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Gross margin increased $584,026 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from the three months ended September 30, 2025 and $1,976,311 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the relocation of the Company’s facility. During 2025, the Company was in the process of relocating operations and as a result, was operating at a limited capacity. Following the completion of the relocation the business returned to normal operating capacity resulting in higher revenue levels and related costs. The year-over-year increase is also impacted by the timing of the common control transaction. The statement of operations for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 includes operating activity from April 16, 2025 only, compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

ga.text: General and Administrative Expenses. General and administrative expense decreased $2,016,516 during the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease is primarily driven by the costs of the share exchange occurring in Q3 2025. General and administrative expenses increased $4,521,058 during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from the nine months ended September 30 2025. The change in general and administrative expenses was attributable to increased compliance costs associated with being a public company including increased spend on investor relations and legal costs. Additionally, the Company incurred approximately $600,000 in costs during 2026 related to the relocation of the RPD site for incremental storage, disposals and assembly fees. This is furthered by the statement of operations only including six months of general and administrative expenses related to the RPD business compared to nine months in 2026.

nonop.text: Other Income (Expense). Other income/expenses, net, totaled ($212,002) and $(442,608) during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $(288,435) and $280,176 during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase quarter over quarter is due to the loss on extinguishment on the HUSA Convertible note incurred during the third quarter of 2025 and the decrease year over year is primarily related to the end of the grant and the related income in 2025 with no similar income receivable in 2026.

Engineering and Process Development Serv.text: As a result of the acquisition of RPD on April 1, 2026 which was accounted for as a common control transaction, the majority of the Company’s revenue is now generated from engineering and process development services. The revenue from these services includes contracts in which revenue is recognized overtime. The application of this accounting policy requires significant management judgement and estimates, including the determination of total expected project costs, progress towards completion and timing of satisfaction of performance obligations. Changes in these estimates could have a material impact on the amount and timing of revenue recognized. As the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 was filed before the acquisition, we have identified revenue recognized over time as a new critical accounting estimate. Progress toward completion is measured using an input method, generally based on cost incurred and labor hours relative to the total estimated costs and labor hours to complete each contract. This method requires management to make significant estimates, including the total expected costs or labor hours to complete each project, the progress toward satisfying each performance obligation, and the amount of consideration expected to be received.

Oil and Gas.text: Revenue- Oil and Gas. The Oil and Gas segment generates revenue from oil and gas operations whereas Renewables is in pre-revenue stage, primarily incurring research and development and start-up costs associated with its development of scalable technologies for converting plastic and biomass waste into renewable fuels and chemicals. Total revenue from the oil and gas segment decreased $71,552 quarter over quarter for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from the three months ended September 30, 2025 due to a decrease in volume of production from the leases. Total revenue increased $204,444 year over year for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to the timing of the Share Exchange, which occurred at the beginning of the third quarter of 2025. As a result, the 2025 period includes only three months of Oil and Gas revenue, compared to nine months in 2026.

intro.text: On July 1, 2025, Abundia Global Impact Group, Inc. (formerly Houston American Energy Corp.), a Delaware corporation (the “Company”), acquired all of the outstanding units of Abundia Global Impact Group, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“AGIG”), as described below (the “Share Exchange”). Prior to the Share Exchange, the Company operated as an independent oil and gas company, which had previously focused on the development, exploration, exploitation, acquisition, and production of natural gas and crude oil properties, with its principal properties and operations located in the U.S. Permian Basin and additional properties in the Louisiana U.S. Gulf Coast region. The Company intends to continue to maintain its legacy oil and gas assets as well as the AGIG business.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Final product offerings and sales volumes will depend on successful facility development, feedstock availability, regulatory approvals, and customer demand.
Commercial sales are expected to depend on successful facility completion, product qualification and regulatory compliance.

We are designing the facility with the objective of operating as a minor source for purposes of air permitting (i.e., maintaining potential emissions below thresholds that would otherwise trigger more stringent major source and operating permit requirements).

Under past proposals, the EPA would issue or sell a capped and steadily declining number of tradable emissions allowances to certain major sources of greenhouse gas emissions so that such sources could continue to emit greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.
Future capital requirements will depend on many factors, including:
Accordingly, we will need to continue to rely on additional financing to achieve our business objectives.
The Company expects to rely on a limited number of industry partners for a significant portion of its near-term revenue.
The Company and other participants in the alternative energy and fuel industry rely on governmental programs requiring or incentivizing the consumption of low carbon fuels.
Additionally, we must often rely on our own market research to forecast sales, as detailed forecasts are not generally obtainable from other sources at this early stage of the industry.
Our success will depend on our ability to maintain a competitive position with respect to technological advances.

The successful implementation of an expense reduction plan, if and when deemed advisable by management, depends on many factors, including our ability to identify the need for such a plan in a timely manner, to effectively implement such a plan, as well as certain factors which are beyond our control, including economic conditions, labor market conditions and ability to maintain its management team to implement the plan.
We rely on a combination of patent, trademark and trade secret protection, confidentiality, nondisclosure and non-use agreements to protect our proprietary rights.

Additionally, for certain of the Company’s existing and future in-licensed patent rights, it may not have the right to bring suit for infringement and may have to rely on third parties to enforce these rights for it.
We rely on trade secrets to protect some of our technology and proprietary information, especially where we believe patent protection is not appropriate or obtainable.

In addition to the protection afforded by patents, we rely on trade secret protection and confidentiality agreements to protect proprietary know-how that is not patentable or that we elect not to patent, processes for which patents are difficult to enforce, and information or technology that is not covered by patents.
The Company depends on certain technologies that are sold or licensed to it.
Our success also will depend upon our ability to attract and retain additional qualified management, marketing, technical, and sales executives and personnel.

We rely on information technology systems to keep financial records and corporate records, communicate with staff and external parties, and operate other critical functions, including sales and manufacturing processes.
The prices we receive for our production depend on numerous factors beyond our control.

The declaration and payment in the future of any cash or stock dividends on our common stock will be at the discretion of our Board and will depend upon a variety of factors, including our future earnings, capital requirements, financial condition and such other factors as our Board may consider to be relevant from time to time.
